clue.text: Penetrative manoeuvres sink chess freak after queen turns on 6th file

indicators.note: in this across clue 'on' means the file letter is placed first, ahead of what follows
after says the scrambled chess letters come behind the turned queen

parts.note: on a chessboard the files run a to h, so the sixth is the f-file

indicators.note: turns tells us the queen's royal cypher is read backwards here

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cypher

indicators.note: freak as a verb means to go wild, so the letters of sink chess are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chess game in which a queen manoeuvre on the f-file makes a chess fanatic go to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess vocabulary is all misdirection. 'turns' gives RE from ER; 'freak' rearranges SINK CHESS into NCHKISSES; F leads and RE follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep kisses with the tongue are playfully described as penetrative manoeuvres, a cheeky euphemism.

clue.text: What happened in the seventh square of 12A and the second square of 21A, let's hope

definitions.text: What happened in the seventh square of 12A and the second square of 21A
definitions.meaning: in the grid, diagonal lines of hidden finger names (index, middle, ring, little) cross at those squares, so digits were literally overlapped there
a phrase said when wishing for good luck

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is about the grid itself: highlighted diagonals spelling finger names intersect in those two squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you are keeping digits overlapped is the idiom for wishing that something turns out well.

clue.text: Compound fracture's terrible bandages

indicators.note: bandages means wraps round, so the letters sought are held within fracture's terrible

explanation.surface: A broken bone of the compound kind is terrible, and so are its dressings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound fracture' reads as one medical phrase, but 'Compound' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically, this is a compound formed from an acid and an alcohol, such as those giving fruit scents.

clue.text: Bureaucrats moving mechanistically to oust cinema complex

indicators.note: moving says the letters of mechanistically are shifted around

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters to rework
taken as written; to oust says these letters are expelled from the pool

explanation.surface: Officials clumsily lumbering about in order to evict a multiplex.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, I, N, E, M, A from MECHANISTICALLY and the leftover nine letters, rearranged by 'moving', give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal headquarters stand by metonymy for the officials and red tape inside them.

clue.text: The Church of Scotland caused King distress

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to distress is to annoy or vex

explanation.surface: The Scottish church once upset the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scots word for a church and the everyday name of the national Presbyterian church in Scotland.

clue.text: Reprobate Viz anticipates some litigation Attorney-General overlooked

indicators.note: anticipates means comes before, so this abbreviation leads
in a down clue, being overlooked means sitting beneath what looks down on it

parts.note: viz (videlicet, 'namely') has the Latin twin scilicet, abbreviated sc
a law, as in going to law, is some litigation

explanation.surface: The comic Viz pre-empts a lawsuit that the government's chief lawyer missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is also a British satirical comic, which is the surface reading; here it is the Latin 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal, an unprincipled scoundrel; this is a variant spelling of scallywag.

clue.text: Windows opening worry emigrant

indicators.note: opening means prising apart, so the Windows letters sit inside the worry word

parts.note: to worry or bother, as in 'what's eating you?'
XP is a version of Microsoft Windows

explanation.surface: A worry about opening Windows, the computer system, bothers someone who has moved abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living outside their native country is an expatriate, shortened in everyday use.

clue.text: One establishing excellent name as a monk?

indicators.note: as a here means being within, as one is when part of a religious brotherhood

parts.note: a monk belongs to a religious order
A1, written AI, means first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone earning a fine reputation as a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a' signals placing within: a monk lives inside his religious brotherhood, so the excellent name goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who ordains decrees or founds something, so is someone setting it up.

clue.text: Runs away square, getting in OK

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: legit is slang for legitimate, all right
S is short for square, as in sq or a map grid's square

explanation.surface: A batsman scampering to square leg and making his ground safely.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for running off hurriedly, fleeing on foot.

clue.text: A riot developing after not quite filling birthing pools

indicators.note: filling means the scrambled letters sit inside the other piece
not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: natal relates to birth

indicators.note: developing means taking new shape, so the letters of a riot are reorganised

explanation.surface: A disturbance breaks out at a maternity unit's birthing pools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birthing pools' looks like one thing, but 'birthing' gives NATA (natal less its end), around ATORI from A RIOT; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natatoria is the plural of natatorium, a swimming bath or indoor swimming facility.

clue.text: Bluish-grey, essentially

definitions.meaning: a dark greyish-blue colour, especially of cloth
the Latin phrase meaning in itself or intrinsically

explanation.definitionFit: One word is a rare colour name; split as two Latin words it means by its own nature.

clue.text: Your old listener, predominantly crude

indicators.note: read as pre-dominantly, it says the listener goes in front

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An archaic voice suggests your ear is mostly coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predominantly' is read as pre-dominantly, so the listener goes in front even though the clue names it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse humour is called earthy or crude, both meaning vulgar and unrefined.

clue.text: Removing south, mobile workers who are out of this world?

definitions.text: who are out of this world?

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mobile, as for a mobile phone number

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so the south letter is cut out

parts.note: artisans are skilled workers

explanation.surface: Travelling labourers being moved on from the south seem alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of the planet Mars, a stock example of aliens from beyond Earth.

clue.text: 'A miss __, perversely, as good as a ____'?

definitions.text: 'A miss __, perversely, as good as a ____'?

indicators.note: perversely means the wrong way round, so the gap's word is turned back

parts.note: the first gap in the saying is filled by the word is
the second gap in the saying is filled by mile

explanation.surface: A proverb with words missing, as in a fill-in-the-blanks quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'A miss is as good as a mile'. Its comparison using 'as good as' is itself an example of the figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech comparing two things with as or like, which the proverb does.

clue.text: Old browser will be the death of him, so Giovanni thinks

indicators.note: the death of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: 'as to Don' means 'so' (regarding the Don), the opinion of Don Giovanni

explanation.surface: Mozart's Don Giovanni fears a ghostly old figure will kill him.
explanation.walkthrough: In the opera, the statue of the Commendatore drags Don Giovanni to hell. 'browser' is not a web browser: it is an animal that feeds on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct elephant-like animal that fed by browsing trees and shrubs, so an ancient leaf-eater.

clue.text: Wine information shared by those who toss up here?

parts.note: Highland games athletes toss a caber, a long tree trunk
the net, the internet, is where information is shared

explanation.surface: Wine tips swapped by people flipping coins here.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland Games event; the clue imagines an online network for those athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: A red grape variety, sauvignon, and the dry red wine made from it.

clue.text: Chopper's mine to attend Her Majesty

parts.note: egg is slang for a mine or bomb
to be at an event is to attend it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cypher

explanation.surface: A man with an axe claims it is his to serve the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a helicopter, from its whirring rotor blades, just as chopper is.

clue.text: Next door, a club entertainer with not much in the hat?

parts.note: a DJ plays records in a nightclub
a single cent is a poor take in a busker's hat

explanation.surface: The neighbour, a nightclub act, collects almost nothing from passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying beside or next to something, as houses in a row are.

clue.text: Removal of intro badly disorientates new part of Manhattan

indicators.note: badly means the letters of disorientates are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters to rework
taken as written; removal of says these letters are taken from the pool

explanation.surface: Cutting a badly placed introduction confuses a newcomer to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I, N, T, R, O from DISORIENTATES; 'badly' rearranges the remaining eight letters. 'new' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upper and Lower districts on the eastern side of the island form a well-known area of the borough.

clue.text: In submitting to British Library, Slim Shady offers badge

indicators.note: submitting to means giving way, so one pair of letters yields its place to another

parts.note: Slim Shady is the alter ego of the rapper Eminem
taken as written
BL is the abbreviation for the British Library

explanation.surface: A rapper donating his material to the national library gets a badge for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a link: it is the letters IN, which give way to BL in EMINEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol or crest that serves as an identifying sign, as a badge does.

clue.text: A composer dumps the European in charge of fungus

indicators.note: dumps means discards, so some letters are thrown out

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer, and the setter's pseudonym
el is 'the' in Spanish, a European language

explanation.surface: A composer quits the EU representative in charge of a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the European' reads like a person but means the word 'the' in a European language: Spanish EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of gilled mushroom, such as the field mushroom or fly agaric.

clue.text: See 1
Lab test watery spot that I'll introduce into another

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: another watery spot, here a bay of the sea

indicators.note: the letter I introduces the word by being moved to its front

parts.note: an oasis is a spot of water in a desert

explanation.surface: A laboratory test on water from one site placed into another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second watery spot; 'that I'll introduce' moves the desert spot's I to its front, giving IOASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientific measurement of a substance's potency by its effect on living tissue, done in a laboratory.

clue.text: Most elementary features column

indicators.note: features means includes as part of itself, so the letters lie inside most elementary

explanation.surface: The most basic design includes a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright stone slab or pillar bearing an inscription, a type of monumental column.

clue.text: Releases 'C'mon Everybody'?

definitions.meaning: frees or stops holding on to something
a rallying cry urging everyone to start, the sense of the song title

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a verb phrase it means drops hold; read as a contraction it is an urge to begin.

clue.text: Ugly lumps taking Northern Line Tube?

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a northward line means reading upwards

parts.note: warts are unsightly growths on the skin

explanation.surface: Unsightly bulges on a London Underground trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northern Line is a London Underground line and 'Tube' the London Underground, but here they mean going north and a drinking pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin hollow stem or plastic pipe for sipping drinks.

clue.text: Roger otherwise engaged in essence

indicators.note: in essence means at the core, so the letters come from within otherwise engaged

explanation.surface: A radio operator acknowledges that someone is busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio-speak 'roger' means message received and understood, the same as saying you follow.

clue.text: Gradually reduce in utero decay

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside utero decay

explanation.surface: Something in the womb wasting away little by little.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away by slow degrees, as water does to rock.

clue.text: Comfortable, settling on these, yes, to indulge in holiday writing?

indicators.note: to indulge in means to get inside, so this letter goes within the holiday

parts.note: Easter is a religious holiday
Y is short for yes, as in a Y/N box
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Relaxing on holiday, agreeing to spend time writing postcards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: generous instalment terms are what one comfortably settles a bill on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire-purchase payment by low instalments, a comfortable way to settle a debt.

clue.text: On the face of it unfriendly visitor from far left the Corporation argued about

definitions.text: On the face of it unfriendly

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the BBC nickname surrounds the visitor and left

parts.note: the Beeb is the nickname of the British Broadcasting Corporation
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the film
rowed, rhyming with cowed, means quarrelled

explanation.surface: An alien from the far left quarrelled with the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far left' looks political, but 'far' belongs to the visitor and 'left' is L.
explanation.definitionFit: Having heavy overhanging eyebrows makes a face look scowling and hostile.
